title: Synapse Labs - Discovery: Migration from OpenAI to Dedicated

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-31 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Synapse CTO), Marcus Lee (Synapse ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Synapse Sec)

Auto-summary: Synapse is evaluating moving from OpenAI hosted endpoints to a Dedicated Redwood deployment for latency predictability and cost control. Main concerns: eval parity, compatibility with their current self-hosted stack (vLLM/TGI), networking and KMS integration, and timeline for a pilot.

[00:00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros?
[00:00:06] Priya (Synapse): Hi, Priya here, CTO at Synapse. Marcus and Sofia are on with me. We're trying to understand migration effort from our OpenAI usage to something more predictable.
[00:00:15] Marcus (Synapse): Yep, hi. We run a mixture of OpenAI and some on-prem vLLM experiments. Latency spikes and cost variability are killing us.
[00:00:00] Arjun (Redwood): Thanks, good context. Quick note - I'll be the SE, I'll ask about prompts and inference shapes. Lena will cover pricing and go-to-market stuff.
[00:00:35] Lena (Redwood): Great. Priya, what's the main driver? Is it cost, data control, latency, or all of the above?
[00:00:41] Priya (Synapse): All of the above, honestly. We have regulatory customers asking for more control over residency and audit logs. And the token bill from OpenAI scaled way beyond expectations.
[00:00:53] Sofia (Synapse): Security's big for us - KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 evidence. We also need to understand what data stays with Redwood versus what hits public networks.
[00:01:05] Lena (Redwood): Understood. On Dedicated we offer VPC peering options and customer KMS integrations - we can discuss HSM later. We also provide audit logs you can ship to your SIEM.
[00:01:18] Marcus (Synapse): Cool. On the model side, we're using GPT-4-ish via OpenAI and some TGI-backed models internally. Compatibility is my worry - will our prompts and evals behave the same on Redwood?
[00:01:31] Arjun (Redwood): Good question. We try to maintain eval parity. Two things: model variant parity (we host compatible open models and Redwood-verified variants) and inference differences if you run quantized kernels or different runtimes like vLLM or TGI.
[00:01:45] Marcus (Synapse): Right, we've seen v-L-L-M - vLLM - produce slightly different tokenization in a couple of edge cases; that's caused eval drift.
[00:01:55] Arjun (Redwood): Yeah, tokenization and temperature seeding can differ. For migration we usually run a small eval suite - your core prompt set - across the source (OpenAI) and our Dedicated instance to measure metric delta.
[00:02:08] Priya (Synapse): How long does that take? Can you automate it?
[00:02:12] Arjun (Redwood): We can run an initial 1-hour benchmark on a p4d or similar; that gives latency percentiles, throughput, and cost per token. We also run quality checks against your eval metrics. We provide a spreadsheet comparing outputs so you can eyeball differences.
[00:02:26] Lena (Redwood): We'll include that as part of the pilot; pricing will include a short trial benchmark discount.
[00:02:33] Marcus (Synapse): About model compatibility - we rely on a couple of open weights running on TGI internally. Would Redwood host those weights or do we need to bring them?
[00:02:43] Arjun (Redwood): We can host customer-provided weights in Private or Dedicated deployments, subject to licensing. For hosted models we surface curated open models; for Dedicated you can pin custom weights or request us to onboard them. There might be kernel/quantization tuning needed.
[00:02:58] Marcus (Synapse): Ok. And with vLLM, sometimes the KV cache behavior is slightly different which affects latency of subsequent tokens - do you have continuous batching and KV cache handling aligned?
[00:03:09] Arjun (Redwood): Our serving runtime has continuous batching and KV cache management. We also tune kernel selection based on sequence length distribution. But yes, we'll validate with your workload since behavior can vary with quantization and sequence patterns.
[00:03:23] Priya (Synapse): What's the lift for networking? We run in an AWS account and want private comms.
[00:03:28] Lena (Redwood): Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private Connect. For Private deployments we do a customer-managed control plane. We'll need a network diagram. Also, egress and S3 access patterns matter for pricing.
[00:03:42] Sofia (Synapse): KMS - we prefer customer-managed CMKs. Any constraints?
[00:03:46] Arjun (Redwood): We support customer KMS integrations and can do envelope encryption. HSM support is on request for private deployments. We'll include a security pack with details.
[00:03:58] Marcus (Synapse): Are there any feature gaps vs OpenAI - e.g., streaming, function calling, chat state?
[00:04:05] Lena (Redwood): We support streaming responses and function/tool calling on our API. For dedicated you can enable the same routes. There may be slight API contract differences if you use OpenAI-specific endpoints; we provide mapping guides.
[00:04:18] Priya (Synapse): Good. Pricing model: how predictable is Dedicated vs hosted? We're comparing per-token with dedicated reserved capacity.
[00:04:26] Lena (Redwood): Hosted is pure usage-based. Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly/annual commits and predictable throughput. We can show modeled cost comparisons using your historical usage. We'll include a worksheet to plug in your numbers.
[00:04:40] Marcus (Synapse): We have spikes during onboarding flows - can you handle bursts?
[00:04:44] Arjun (Redwood): Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. For very spiky workloads we recommend a hybrid routing policy - route low-latency critical traffic to Dedicated and fallback to hosted in overload scenarios.
[00:04:58] Sofia (Synapse): SLA and monitoring? We need token-level audit, per-route metrics, and retention policy options for logs.
[00:05:06] Lena (Redwood): Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and you can export traces. Log retention add-ons are available for enterprise.
[00:05:13] Marcus (Synapse): About migration sequence - what's the recommended path?
[00:05:17] Arjun (Redwood): Typical: 1) Run parity benchmarks on a Dedicated instance with your eval set; 2) Tweak quantization and runtime configs for parity; 3) Start a canary rollout for a subset of traffic, compare business metrics; 4) Full cutover with rollback policies.
[00:05:31] Priya (Synapse): Timeline - could we pilot in 3-6 weeks?
[00:05:35] Lena (Redwood): Yes, with a quick benchmark and a short pilot we can be in that window.
[00:05:39] Marcus (Synapse): One more question - we also run some models in an on-prem TGI cluster. Is there an option for a Private deployment that syncs model configs so devs have consistent APIs across infra?
[00:05:50] Arjun (Redwood): Yes, our Private deployment is designed for that: same API and config layer across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so you can pin model versions and rollout policies consistently.
[00:05:59] Priya (Synapse): Potential blockers? Anything that has tripped other customers?
[00:06:03] Arjun (Redwood): Usually tokenization edge cases, licensing for certain weights, and network configuration are the main items. We'll surface those during the benchmark.
[00:06:12] Marcus (Synapse): For eval parity, can you add a human review step? Some of our metrics are nuanced.
[00:06:17] Arjun (Redwood): Absolutely - our quality monitoring integrates with eval sets and we can attach human review samples. We'll share a spreadsheet with side-by-side outputs.
[00:06:26] Sofia (Synapse): Also want to confirm SSO/SAML and RBAC options so engineers get least-priv access.
[00:06:31] Lena (Redwood): We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls in the console. We'll include admin onboarding docs.
[00:06:40] Priya (Synapse): Great. Anything else on technical constraints? Marcus?
[00:06:44] Marcus (Synapse): We're good for now. We'll send the prompt/eval set after this call.
[00:06:50] Lena (Redwood): Awesome. I'll send pricing + security pack and loop Arjun for the benchmark.
[00:06:55] Arjun (Redwood): Quick note on benchmarking: please include typical sequence lengths and concurrency targets. That changes kernel selection.
[00:07:03] Marcus (Synapse): Will do - avg seq length about 280 tokens, 99th around 1,200, concurrency varies 50-200 depending on flow.
[00:07:14] Priya (Synapse): We're sensitive to latency P99 under 500ms for critical flows.
[00:07:18] Arjun (Redwood): Noted. We'll aim to report p50/p95/p99 in the benchmark and a cost per 1M tokens estimate.
[00:07:26] Lena (Redwood): Ok, let's recap next steps...
[00:07:29] Lena (Redwood): Lena to send Dedicated pricing, SOC2 summary, networking checklist, and S3/egress worksheet. Arjun to run 1-hour perf benchmark once they share prompts and seq stats. Synapse to share prompt set and security requirements.
[00:07:45] Priya (Synapse): Sounds good. We'll aim to have docs over by next week.
[00:07:49] Marcus (Synapse): One last thing - do you have any public benchmark links or case studies?
[00:07:53] Lena (Redwood): Yes, we'll include a link to our benchmark deck and a reference case study (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks and internal doc: drive:Synapse_example).
[00:08:02] Sofia (Synapse): Perfect. Thanks all.
[00:08:05] Lena (Redwood): Thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with short bits of wrap-up and scheduling)

End of call
